key_facts: July 3, 2026 update: Michigan remains the clear national epicenter with >300 confirmed cyclosporiasis cases as of Thursday afternoon July 2 (MDHHS to ABC News/CBS Detroit; up from 174 June 30 -> 228 July 1 across 22 jurisdictions incl. Monroe 92, Lenawee 36, Washtenaw 28, Wayne 17 -> ~+100 Thursday; Dr. Natasha Bagdasarian expects further rise given 1-2 week incubation). WXYZ (July 2) confirmed MDHHS is actively sharing data with CDC and MDARD. CDC seasonal page still reflects May 1-June 15/16 onsets (145 U.S.-acquired across 17 states excl. Michigan: NY 31-80, IL 11-30, TX 11-30, 14 states 1-10) with no July 3 holiday update. NBC Chicago (July 3) highlighted Michigan as the Midwest epicenter with no Illinois surge; no competing July 2-3 outbreak alerts in TX, NY, FL, or OH (Lucas County OH was ~65 July 1). Raised Michigan 0.78 -> 0.82 as active MDHHS->CDC data sharing and shrinking reporting window ahead of CDC NNDSS/mid-July tables ahead of July 16 strengthen MI lead; New York 0.09 remains primary CDC publication/reporting-lag hedge, Texas 0.04, Ohio 0.03, Illinois 0.01.
